# Minutes worked per period

Source: https://docs.timefold.ai/employee-shift-scheduling/1.28.x/employee-resource-constraints/work-limits/minutes-worked-per-period.html

# Minutes worked per period

There are different techniques for managing employees' working hours.

A period can be defined as a week, month, or the entire schedule.

This guide explains managing employees' hours with minutes worked per period:

| ## Learn how to configure an API Key to run the examples in this guide:
 In the examples, replace  | 

Period rules are defined in contracts:

```
{
  "contracts": [
    {
      "id": "partTimeContract",
      "periodRules": [
        {
          "id": "Max8HoursPerDay",
          "period": "DAY",
          "satisfiability": "REQUIRED",
          "minutesWorkedLimit": {
            "minutesWorkedMax": 480
          }
        },
        {
          "id": "Max32HoursPerWeek",
          "period": "WEEK",
          "satisfiability": "REQUIRED",
          "minutesWorkedLimit": {
            "minutesWorkedMax": 1920
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
Period rules define how many minutes employees work in a given period. For instance, 480 minutes (8 hours) per day or 1,920 minutes (32 hours) per week.

`PeriodRules` must include an ID.

`period` sets the period the rule applies to, for instance, `DAY`, `WEEK`, `MONTH`, `SCHEDULE`.

## Further information about `period`:

`DAY` spans a single day and occurs every day in the schedule.

`WEEK` spans 7 days and occurs every week (including partial weeks) in the schedule.
The default start of the week is Monday, but this can be overridden to any day in the week:

```
{
  "scheduleParameterization": {
    "weekStart": "THURSDAY"
  }
}
```
`MONTH` spans the entire month.
`MONTH` has a variable number of days depending on the days in the month and occurs every month (including partial months) in the schedule.

`SCHEDULE` spans the entire schedule.

| You can define custom periods to apply to this rule in the following way: | 

```
{
  "scheduleParameterization": {
    "periods": [
      {
        "id": "PAY_PERIOD",
        "dateSpans": [
          {
            "start": "2023-01-01",
            "end": "2023-01-15"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```
The `start` and `end` dates are inclusive.

## Learn about counting days in rules:

By default, rules count shifts within the defined period or rolling window if the shift starts within it. For instance, if you define a rule that an employee can only work one shift per day, a night shift that started on the previous day but ends the following morning will not be counted towards the limits specified in the rule.

To change this behavior, change the field `periodShiftOverlapKind` from `START_ONLY` to `START_AND_END`.

- 
Period rule 
- 
Rolling-window rule 

```
{
  "periodRules": [
    {
      "id": "Max8HoursPerDayFullTime",
      "period": "DAY",
      "minutesWorkedLimit": {
        "minutesWorkedMax": 480
      },
      "satisfiability": "REQUIRED",
      "periodShiftOverlapKind": "START_AND_END"
    }
  ]
}
```
```
{
  "rollingWindowRules": [
    {
      "id": "Max8HoursPerDayRolling",
      "rollingWindow": {
        "type": "DAILY",
        "size": 1
      },
      "minutesWorkedLimit": {
        "minutesWorkedMax": 480
      },
      "satisfiability": "REQUIRED",
      "periodShiftOverlapKind": "START_AND_END"
    }
  ]
}
```
This makes the rule count all parts of shifts that overlap with the defined period or rolling window. In the previous example, the night shift starts on the previous day and ends the following morning. With `START_AND_END`, the portion of the night shift that overlaps the target period or window is counted toward the rule.

The default behavior of all rules when this field is not specified is `START_ONLY`.

`minutesWorkedLimit.minutesWorkedMax` sets the limit on how many minutes the employee can work in the specified period.

By default, breaks in shifts do not count towards working time. It is possible to specify which breaks are subtracted from working time for the rule by using `unloggedBreakTags`.

## Further information about subtracting breaks from working time based on tags:

Breaks with specific tags are not logged towards the working time of this rule. Tags are defined in shift breaks:

```
{
  "shifts": [
    {
      "id": "shift 1",
      "start": "2027-02-01T09:00:00Z",
      "end": "2027-02-01T18:00:00Z",
      "breaks": [
        {
          "start": "2027-02-01T10:30:00Z",
          "end": "2027-02-01T10:45:00Z",
          "tags": ["teaBreak"]
        },
        {
          "start": "2027-02-01T12:00:00Z",
          "end": "2027-02-01T13:00:00Z",
          "tags": ["lunchBreak"]
        },
        {
          "start": "2027-02-01T16:30:00Z",
          "end": "2027-02-01T16:45:00Z",
          "tags": ["teaBreak"]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
Use `unloggedBreakTags` to specify which breaks are subtracted from the working time for this rule.
Breaks which do not match the tags will be counted as working time.
Do not use this field if all breaks must be subtracted from working time, regardless of their tags.

`breakTagMatches` can be set to `ALL` or `ANY`.
The default behavior for `breakTagMatches` is `ALL`, and if omitted, the default `ALL` will be used.

The rule can define only `unloggedBreakTags`.

```
{
  "unloggedBreakTags": ["lunchBreak"],
  "breakTagMatches": "ALL"
}
```
In the above example, breaks which have the tag `lunchBreak` will be subtracted from working time for the rule. All other breaks will count as working time.

With `breakTagMatches` set to `ALL`, all tags defined by the rule’s `unloggedBreakTags` attribute must be present in the break in order for it to be subtracted from working time.
With `breakTagMatches` set to `ANY`, at least one tag defined by the rule’s `unloggedBreakTags` attribute must be present in the break.

| In some situations it is necessary to specify rules that apply to both the day and the week. If a rule for the week is included that sets a maximum number of hours per week at 40, but no rule is included for the day period, an employee could be assigned continuous shifts for 40 hours and then nothing for the rest of the week. Similarly, if a rule is included that sets a maximum number of hours per day at 8, but no rule is included for the week, an employee could be assigned an 8-hour shift every single day with no days off. | 

Each employee must specify which contracts apply to them:

```
{
  "employees": [
    {
      "id": "Ann",
      "contracts": [
        "partTimeContract"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
`periodRules` can include or exclude shifts based on shift tags.

```
{
  "periodRules": [
    {
      "id": "Max8HoursPerDay",
      "period": "DAY",
      "satisfiability": "REQUIRED",
      "includeShiftTags": ["Part-time"],
      "shiftTagMatches": "ALL",
      "minutesWorkedLimit": {
        "minutesWorkedMax": 480
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
## Further information about including or excluding shifts with shift tags:

Shifts with specific tags can be included or excluded by the rule. Tags are defined in shifts:

```
{
  "shifts": [
    {
      "id": "2027-02-01",
      "start": "2027-02-01T09:00:00Z",
      "end": "2027-02-01T17:00:00Z",
      "tags": ["Part-time"]
    }
  ]
}
```
Use `includeShiftTags` to include shifts with specific tags or  `excludeShiftTags` to exclude shifts with specific tags.

`shiftTagMatches` can be set to `ALL` or `ANY`.
The default behavior for `shiftTagMatches` is `ALL`, and if omitted, the default `ALL` will be used.

The rule can define either `includeShiftTags` or `excludeShiftTags`, but not both.

```
{
  "includeShiftTags": ["Part-time", "Weekend"],
  "shiftTagMatches": "ALL"
}
```
With `shiftTagMatches` set to `ALL`, all tags defined by the rule’s `includeShiftTags` attribute must be present in the shift. With `shiftTagMatches` set to `ANY`, at least one tag defined by the rule’s `includeShiftTags` attribute must be present in the shift.

```
{
  "excludeShiftTags": ["Part-time", "Weekend"],
  "shiftTagMatches": "ALL"
}
```
With `shiftTagMatches` set to `ALL`, all tags defined by the rule’s `excludeShiftTags` attribute cannot be present in the shift.
This is useful when you want to exclude things in combination with each other.
For instance, excluding the shift tags `Part-time` and `Weekend` with `shiftTagMatches` set to `All`, will exclude shifts that include the tags `Part-time` and `Weekend` from the rule.
Shifts tagged only `Part-time` or only `Weekend` will not be excluded.

With `shiftTagMatches` set to `ANY`, any of the tags defined by the rule’s `excludeShiftTags` attribute cannot be present in the shift.
This is useful when you need to exclude tags regardless of their relationship to other tags.
For instance, excluding the shift tags `Part-time` and `Weekend` with `shiftTagMatches` set to `ANY`, will exclude any shift that includes the tags `Part-time` or `Weekend`, whether they occur together or not.

`periodRules` can count only the portion of shifts that overlap with a specific daily time interval using `minutesWorkedLimit.countOnlyBetween`.
This is useful for limiting hours worked during specific times of day, such as night shifts.

```
{
  "periodRules": [
    {
      "id": "Max38HoursNightWorkPerWeek",
      "period": "WEEK",
      "satisfiability": "REQUIRED",
      "minutesWorkedLimit": {
        "minutesWorkedMax": 2280,
        "countOnlyBetween": {
          "start": "00:00",
          "end": "06:00"
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
The `countOnlyBetween` interval specifies:

- 
`start`: The start time of the daily interval (inclusive).
- 
`end`: The end time of the daily interval (exclusive). If`end`is less than`start`, the interval spans midnight into the next day (e.g.,`22:00`to`06:00`).

Time is interpreted in the employee’s time zone. For multi-day shifts, the overlap is calculated for each day.

When the satisfiability of the rule is `REQUIRED`, the `Minutes worked per period not in required range for employee` hard constraint is invoked, which makes sure the number of minutes worked doesn’t exceed the limit specified in `minutesWorkedMax`.

Shifts will be left unassigned if assigning them would break the `Minutes worked per period not in required range for employee` constraint.

In the following example, there are 5 shifts, 1 employee, and a rule with a required satisfiability that specifies the employee can work at most 1,920 minutes (32 hours) per week.

4 shifts, totaling 1,920 minutes, are assigned and 1 shift is left unassigned to avoid breaking the `Minutes worked per period not in required range for employee` hard constraint.

When the satisfiability of the rule is `PREFERRED`, the `Minutes worked per period not in preferred range for employee` soft constraint is invoked.

With a satisfiability of `PREFERRED` a `minutesWorkedLimit.minutesWorkedMin` value can also be provided to set the preferred minimum number of minutes worked.

| `REQUIRED`satisfiability is not supported with`minutesWorkedLimit.minutesWorkedMin`. | 

```
{
  "contracts": [
    {
      "id": "partTimeContract",
      "periodRules": [
        {
          "id": "Min2HoursMax8HoursPerDay",
          "period": "DAY",
          "satisfiability": "PREFERRED",
          "minutesWorkedLimit": {
            "minutesWorkedMin": 120,
            "minutesWorkedMax": 480
          }
        },

          "id": "Min16Max32HoursPerWeek",
          "period": "WEEK",
          "satisfiability": "PREFERRED",

            "minutesWorkedMax": 1920
          }
        }

    }
  ]
}
```

The constraint adds a soft penalty to the dataset score when this preferred range is violated. The penalty is the minutes outside the preferred range multiplied by the employee priority multiplier and the contract’s priority weight, incentivizing Timefold to keep worked minutes within the preferred bounds.

Shifts will still be assigned even if assigning them breaks this constraint.

| Every soft constraint has a weight that can be configured to change the relative importance of the constraint compared to other constraints. | 

| This rule is more likely to be satisfied for employees with a higher employee priority.
See [Employee priority](https://docs.timefold.ai/employee-priority)for more details. | 

In the following example, there are 5 shifts, 1 employee, and a rule with a preferred satisfiability that specifies the employee should only work 1920 minutes (32 hours) per week.

All 5 shifts are assigned, totaling 2,400 minutes, and a soft penalty is applied to the dataset score.

Rules with a satisfiability of `REQUIRED` put a hard limit on how much work employees can be assigned (minutes, hours, days, shifts), and doesn’t assign overtime.

A rule with a satisfiability of `REQUIRED` that states an employee can work a maximum of 1920 minutes worked per period, will never assign the employee more than 1920 minutes worked per period, even if assigning overtime would be beneficial to the overall schedule.

To allow for the possibility of overtime, use rules with a satisfiability of `PREFERRED`.

Set a rule with a `PREFERRED` satisfiability for the maximum number of minutes worked per period.
Now, a rule with a satisfiability of `PREFERRED` that states an employee can preferably work a maximum of 1920 minutes worked per period will allow the employee to be assigned more minutes worked per period (overtime) than specified by the rule when it is necessary to do so.

To place a limit on the total amount of overtime employees can be assigned, include both:

- 
A rule with `PREFERRED`satisfiability for the maximum number of minutes worked per period that is equivalent to the employees normal minutes worked per period.
- 
A rule with `REQUIRED`satisfiability for the maximum number of minutes worked per period (regular hours plus overtime).

The difference between the `PREFERRED` maximum minutes worked per period and `REQUIRED` maximum minutes worked per period is the total amount of overtime that can be assigned to employees.

# Shifts worked in a rolling window

Source: https://docs.timefold.ai/employee-shift-scheduling/1.28.x/employee-resource-constraints/work-limits/shifts-worked-in-a-rolling-window.html

# Shifts worked in a rolling window

There are different techniques for managing employees working hours.

Rolling windows can be defined as hourly, daily, or weekly.

This guide shows you how to manage employees' hours with shifts worked in a rolling window:

| ## Learn how to configure an API Key to run the examples in this guide:
 In the examples, replace  | 

Rolling window rules are defined in contracts:

```
{
  "contracts": [
    {
      "id": "fullTimeContract",
      "rollingWindowRules": [
        {
          "id": "max5ShiftsRollingWindow",
          "rollingWindow": {
            "type": "DAILY",
            "size": 7
          },
          "shiftsWorkedLimit":
          {
            "shiftsWorkedMax": 5
          },
          "satisfiability": "REQUIRED"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
You can define as many `rollingWindowRules` as required.

`rollingWindowRules` must include an ID.

`rollingWindow` specifies the `type` and `size` of the window.

## Further information about `rollingWindows`:

`size` sets how many instances of `type` are included in the rolling window, for instance, the following example specifies a rolling window of 7 days.

```
{
  "rollingWindow": {
    "type": "DAILY",
    "size": 7
  }
}
```
There are three types of rolling windows `HOURLY`, `DAILY`, and `WEEKLY`.

The type specifies how the rolling window progress, hour-by-hour, day-by-day, or week-by-week.

- 
`HOURLY`spans the number of hours specified in`size`and occurs every hour when shifts are scheduled. The hourly window starts when a shift starts (for example 8:00, or 14:30)
- 
`DAILY`spans the number of days specified in`size`for 24-hour periods and covers the entire schedule. The daily window starts at the beginning of a calendar day (midnight).
- 
`WEEKLY`spans the number of weeks specified in`size`and occurs every week (including partial weeks) in the schedule. The weekly window starts at the beginning of a calendar week (usually Monday, or Sunday).

By default, the start of the week is Monday, however, this can be overridden for the entire schedule:

```
{
  "scheduleParameterization": {
    "weekStart": "THURSDAY"
  }
}
```
| Changing `weekStart`is a global change that applies to the entire dataset. | 

The `shiftsWorkedLimit` object must include `shiftsWorkedMax` with the maximum number of shifts to work in the rolling window.

## Learn about counting days in rules:

By default, rules count shifts within the defined period or rolling window if the shift starts within it. For instance, if you define a rule that an employee can only work one shift per day, a night shift that started on the previous day but ends the following morning will not be counted towards the limits specified in the rule.

To change this behavior, change the field `periodShiftOverlapKind` from `START_ONLY` to `START_AND_END`.

- 
Period rule 
- 
Rolling-window rule 

```
{
  "periodRules": [
    {
      "id": "Max8HoursPerDayFullTime",
      "period": "DAY",
      "minutesWorkedLimit": {
        "minutesWorkedMax": 480
      },
      "satisfiability": "REQUIRED",
      "periodShiftOverlapKind": "START_AND_END"
    }
  ]
}
```
```
{
  "rollingWindowRules": [
    {
      "id": "Max8HoursPerDayRolling",
      "rollingWindow": {
        "type": "DAILY",
        "size": 1
      },
      "minutesWorkedLimit": {
        "minutesWorkedMax": 480
      },
      "satisfiability": "REQUIRED",
      "periodShiftOverlapKind": "START_AND_END"
    }
  ]
}
```
This makes the rule count all parts of shifts that overlap with the defined period or rolling window. In the previous example, the night shift starts on the previous day and ends the following morning. With `START_AND_END`, the portion of the night shift that overlaps the target period or window is counted toward the rule.

The default behavior of all rules when this field is not specified is `START_ONLY`.

`RollingWindowRules` can include or exclude shifts based on tags.

```
{
  "rollingWindowRules": [
    {
      "id": "max5ShiftsRollingWindow",
      "includeShiftTags": ["Part-time"],
      "shiftTagMatches": "ALL",
      "rollingWindow": {
        "type": "DAILY",
        "size": 7
      },
      "shiftsWorkedLimit":
      {
        "shiftsWorkedMax": 5
      },
      "satisfiability": "REQUIRED"
    }
  ]
}
```
## Further information about including or excluding shifts with shift tags:

Shifts with specific tags can be included or excluded by the rule. Tags are defined in shifts:

```
{
  "shifts": [
    {
      "id": "2027-02-01",
      "start": "2027-02-01T09:00:00Z",
      "end": "2027-02-01T17:00:00Z",
      "tags": ["Part-time"]
    }
  ]
}
```
Use `includeShiftTags` to include shifts with specific tags or  `excludeShiftTags` to exclude shifts with specific tags.

`shiftTagMatches` can be set to `ALL` or `ANY`.
The default behavior for `shiftTagMatches` is `ALL`, and if omitted, the default `ALL` will be used.

The rule can define either `includeShiftTags` or `excludeShiftTags`, but not both.

```
{
  "includeShiftTags": ["Part-time", "Weekend"],
  "shiftTagMatches": "ALL"
}
```
With `shiftTagMatches` set to `ALL`, all tags defined by the rule’s `includeShiftTags` attribute must be present in the shift. With `shiftTagMatches` set to `ANY`, at least one tag defined by the rule’s `includeShiftTags` attribute must be present in the shift.

```
{
  "excludeShiftTags": ["Part-time", "Weekend"],
  "shiftTagMatches": "ALL"
}
```
With `shiftTagMatches` set to `ALL`, all tags defined by the rule’s `excludeShiftTags` attribute cannot be present in the shift.
This is useful when you want to exclude things in combination with each other.
For instance, excluding the shift tags `Part-time` and `Weekend` with `shiftTagMatches` set to `All`, will exclude shifts that include the tags `Part-time` and `Weekend` from the rule.
Shifts tagged only `Part-time` or only `Weekend` will not be excluded.

With `shiftTagMatches` set to `ANY`, any of the tags defined by the rule’s `excludeShiftTags` attribute cannot be present in the shift.
This is useful when you need to exclude tags regardless of their relationship to other tags.
For instance, excluding the shift tags `Part-time` and `Weekend` with `shiftTagMatches` set to `ANY`, will exclude any shift that includes the tags `Part-time` or `Weekend`, whether they occur together or not.

When the satisfiability of the rule is `REQUIRED`, the `Shifts worked in rolling window not in required range for employee` hard constraint is invoked, which makes sure the number of shifts worked is not above the limit specified in `shiftsWorkedMax`.

Shifts will be left unassigned if assigning them would break the `Shifts worked in rolling window not in required range for employee` constraint.

In the following example, there are 7 shifts, 1 employee, and a rule with a required satisfiability that states the employee cannot work more than 5 shifts in a 7-day rolling window.

5 shifts are assigned, and 2 shifts are left unassigned to avoid breaking the `Shifts worked in rolling window not in required range for employee` hard constraint.

When the satisfiability of the rule is `PREFERRED`, the `Shifts worked in rolling window not in preferred range for employee` soft constraint is invoked.

```
{
  "contracts": [
    {
      "id": "fullTimeContract",
      "rollingWindowRules": [
        {
          "id": "max5ShiftsRollingWindow",

            "size": 7

            "shiftsWorkedMax": 5
          },

        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
The `Shifts worked in rolling window not in preferred range for employee` soft constraint is invoked when `satisfiability` is `PREFERRED` and the number of shifts worked within the rolling window exceeds `shiftsWorkedMax`.

The constraint adds a soft penalty to the dataset score that is calculated as the number of shifts above `shiftsWorkedMax` in the window multiplied by the employee priority multiplier and the contract’s priority weight, normalized to minutes, incentivizing Timefold to keep the shift count within the preferred limit.

Shifts will still be assigned even if assigning them breaks this constraint.

| Every soft constraint has a weight that can be configured to change the relative importance of the constraint compared to other constraints. | 

| This rule is more likely to be satisfied for employees with a higher employee priority.
See [Employee priority](https://docs.timefold.ai/employee-priority)for more details. | 

In the following example, there are 7 shifts, 1 employee, and a rule with a preferred satisfiability that states the employee should not work more than 5 shifts in a 7-day rolling window.

All 7 shifts are assigned, Ann works more than 5 shifts, and a soft penalty is applied to the dataset score.

Rules with a satisfiability of `REQUIRED` put a hard limit on how much work employees can be assigned (minutes, hours, days, shifts), and doesn’t assign overtime.

A rule with a satisfiability of `REQUIRED` that states an employee can work a maximum of 5 shifts in a rolling window, will never assign the employee more than 5 shifts in a rolling window, even if assigning overtime would be beneficial to the overall schedule.

To allow for the possibility of overtime, use rules with a satisfiability of `PREFERRED`.

Set a rule with a `PREFERRED` satisfiability for the maximum number of shifts in a rolling window.
Now, a rule with a satisfiability of `PREFERRED` that states an employee can preferably work a maximum of 5 shifts in a rolling window will allow the employee to be assigned more shifts in a rolling window (overtime) than specified by the rule when it is necessary to do so.

To place a limit on the total amount of overtime employees can be assigned, include both:

- 
A rule with `PREFERRED`satisfiability for the maximum number of shifts in a rolling window that is equivalent to the employees normal shifts in a rolling window.
- 
A rule with `REQUIRED`satisfiability for the maximum number of shifts in a rolling window (regular hours plus overtime).

The difference between the `PREFERRED` maximum shifts in a rolling window and `REQUIRED` maximum shifts in a rolling window is the total amount of overtime that can be assigned to employees.

You can define a condition that has to be fulfilled in the rolling window before the rolling window rule is evaluated.

`condition` specifies the `triggerLimit`, `type` and `includeShiftTags`.

## Further information about `conditions`:

`type` sets the `triggerLimit` unit, for instance, the example below requires at least two shifts to be worked with the tag `Night shift` in the rolling window before the condition is activated.
The `type` can either be `MIN_SHIFTS_WORKED` or `MIN_MINUTES_WORKED`.

```
{
  "condition": {
    "triggerLimit": 2,
    "type": "MIN_SHIFTS_WORKED"
  }
}
```
`includeShiftTags` can be used to only include specific shifts. The example below limits the two shifts worked to "night shifts".

```
{
  "condition": {
    "triggerLimit": 2,
    "type": "MIN_SHIFTS_WORKED",
    "includeShiftTags": [ "Night shift" ]
  }
}
```
For example, an employee must work at most four shifts in a rolling window, if they worked at least one night shift in that rolling window.

```
{
  "contracts": [
    {
      "id": "limitShiftsWhenNightShiftWasWorked",
      "rollingWindowRules": [
        {
          "id": "4ShiftsWorkedRollingWindow",
          "rollingWindow": {
            "type": "WEEKLY",
            "size": 1
          },
          "shiftsWorkedLimit": {
            "shiftsWorkedMax": 4
          },
          "satisfiability": "REQUIRED",
          "condition": {
            "triggerLimit": 1,
            "type": "MIN_SHIFTS_WORKED",
            "includeShiftTags": [ "night shift" ]
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

# Shifts worked per period

Source: https://docs.timefold.ai/employee-shift-scheduling/1.28.x/employee-resource-constraints/work-limits/shifts-worked-per-period.html

# Shifts worked per period

There are different techniques for managing employees working hours.

A period can be defined as a week, month, or the entire schedule.

This guide explains managing employees' hours with shifts worked per period:

| ## Learn how to configure an API Key to run the examples in this guide:
 In the examples, replace  | 

Period rules can define how many shifts employees work in a given period. For instance, a maximum of 4 shifts per week.

| "Days worked rules" and "shifts worked rules" are similar, however, many industries schedule employees multiple shifts per day or spilt shifts. Days worked rules are appropriate when employees are never assigned more than a single shift in a day, however, shifts worked rules are suitable when multiple shifts might be assigned on the same day. | 

Each employee must specify which contracts apply to them:

```
{
  "employees": [
    {
      "id": "Ann",
      "contracts": [
        "fullTimeContract"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
Period rules are configured in contracts:

```
{
  "contracts": [
    {
      "id": "fullTimeContract",
      "periodRules": [
        {
          "id": "Max4ShiftsPerWeek",
          "satisfiability": "REQUIRED",
          "period": "WEEK",
          "shiftsWorkedMax": 4
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
`PeriodRules` must include an ID.

`period` sets the period the rule applies to, for instance, `DAY`, `WEEK`, `MONTH`, `SCHEDULE`.

## Further information about `period`:

`DAY` spans a single day and occurs every day in the schedule.

`WEEK` spans 7 days and occurs every week (including partial weeks) in the schedule.
The default start of the week is Monday, but this can be overridden to any day in the week:

```
{
  "scheduleParameterization": {
    "weekStart": "THURSDAY"
  }
}
```
`MONTH` spans the entire month.
`MONTH` has a variable number of days depending on the days in the month and occurs every month (including partial months) in the schedule.

`SCHEDULE` spans the entire schedule.

| You can define custom periods to apply to this rule in the following way: | 

```
{
  "scheduleParameterization": {
    "periods": [
      {
        "id": "PAY_PERIOD",
        "dateSpans": [
          {
            "start": "2023-01-01",
            "end": "2023-01-15"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```
The `start` and `end` dates are inclusive.

## Learn about counting days in rules:

By default, rules count shifts within the defined period or rolling window if the shift starts within it. For instance, if you define a rule that an employee can only work one shift per day, a night shift that started on the previous day but ends the following morning will not be counted towards the limits specified in the rule.

To change this behavior, change the field `periodShiftOverlapKind` from `START_ONLY` to `START_AND_END`.

- 
Period rule 
- 
Rolling-window rule 

```
{
  "periodRules": [
    {
      "id": "Max8HoursPerDayFullTime",
      "period": "DAY",
      "minutesWorkedLimit": {
        "minutesWorkedMax": 480
      },
      "satisfiability": "REQUIRED",
      "periodShiftOverlapKind": "START_AND_END"
    }
  ]
}
```
```
{
  "rollingWindowRules": [
    {
      "id": "Max8HoursPerDayRolling",
      "rollingWindow": {
        "type": "DAILY",
        "size": 1
      },
      "minutesWorkedLimit": {
        "minutesWorkedMax": 480
      },
      "satisfiability": "REQUIRED",
      "periodShiftOverlapKind": "START_AND_END"
    }
  ]
}
```
This makes the rule count all parts of shifts that overlap with the defined period or rolling window. In the previous example, the night shift starts on the previous day and ends the following morning. With `START_AND_END`, the portion of the night shift that overlaps the target period or window is counted toward the rule.

The default behavior of all rules when this field is not specified is `START_ONLY`.

`shiftsWorkedMax` sets the maximum number of shifts the employee can work in the specified period.

`periodRules` can include or exclude shifts based on shift tags.

```
{
  "periodRules": [
    {
      "id": "fullTimeContract",
      "periodRules": [
        {
          "id": "Max4ShiftsPerWeek",
          "satisfiability": "REQUIRED",
          "period": "WEEK",
          "shiftsWorkedMax": 4,
          "includeShiftTags": ["Part-time"],
          "shiftTagMatches": "ALL"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
## Further information about including or excluding shifts with shift tags:

Shifts with specific tags can be included or excluded by the rule. Tags are defined in shifts:

```
{
  "shifts": [
    {
      "id": "2027-02-01",
      "start": "2027-02-01T09:00:00Z",
      "end": "2027-02-01T17:00:00Z",
      "tags": ["Part-time"]
    }
  ]
}
```
Use `includeShiftTags` to include shifts with specific tags or  `excludeShiftTags` to exclude shifts with specific tags.

`shiftTagMatches` can be set to `ALL` or `ANY`.
The default behavior for `shiftTagMatches` is `ALL`, and if omitted, the default `ALL` will be used.

The rule can define either `includeShiftTags` or `excludeShiftTags`, but not both.

```
{
  "includeShiftTags": ["Part-time", "Weekend"],
  "shiftTagMatches": "ALL"
}
```
With `shiftTagMatches` set to `ALL`, all tags defined by the rule’s `includeShiftTags` attribute must be present in the shift. With `shiftTagMatches` set to `ANY`, at least one tag defined by the rule’s `includeShiftTags` attribute must be present in the shift.

```
{
  "excludeShiftTags": ["Part-time", "Weekend"],
  "shiftTagMatches": "ALL"
}
```
With `shiftTagMatches` set to `ALL`, all tags defined by the rule’s `excludeShiftTags` attribute cannot be present in the shift.
This is useful when you want to exclude things in combination with each other.
For instance, excluding the shift tags `Part-time` and `Weekend` with `shiftTagMatches` set to `All`, will exclude shifts that include the tags `Part-time` and `Weekend` from the rule.
Shifts tagged only `Part-time` or only `Weekend` will not be excluded.

With `shiftTagMatches` set to `ANY`, any of the tags defined by the rule’s `excludeShiftTags` attribute cannot be present in the shift.
This is useful when you need to exclude tags regardless of their relationship to other tags.
For instance, excluding the shift tags `Part-time` and `Weekend` with `shiftTagMatches` set to `ANY`, will exclude any shift that includes the tags `Part-time` or `Weekend`, whether they occur together or not.

The `satisfiability` of the rule can be `REQUIRED` or `PREFERRED`.
`REQUIRED` is the default if omitted.

When the `satisfiability` of the rule is `REQUIRED`, the `Shifts worked per period not in required range for employee` hard constraint is invoked, which makes sure the number of shifts worked does not exceed the limit specified in `shiftsWorkedMax`.

Shifts will be left unassigned if assigning them would break the `Shifts worked per period not in required range for employee` hard constraint.

In the following example, there are 10 shifts and 2 employees.
Ann and Beth both work a maximum of 4 shifts each.
Ann is assigned 4 shifts, Beth is assigned 4 shifts, and 2 shifts are left unassigned to avoid breaking the `Shifts worked per period not in required range for employee` hard constrain.

        "id": "Mon AM",
        "employee": "Ann"
      },
      {
        "id": "Mon PM",
        "employee": "Ann"
      },
      {
        "id": "Tue AM",
        "employee": "Ann"
      },
      {
        "id": "Tue PM",
        "employee": "Ann"
      },
      {
        "id": "Wed AM",
        "employee": "Beth"
      },
      {
        "id": "Wed PM",
        "employee": "Beth"
      },
      {
        "id": "Thu AM",
        "employee": "Beth"
      },
      {
        "id": "Thu PM",
        "employee": "Beth"
      },

      },
      {
        "id": "Fri PM"
      }
    ]
  },

    "employees": 2,
    "shifts": 10,
    "pinnedShifts": 0
  },
  "kpis": {
    "assignedShifts": 8,
    "unassignedShifts": 2,
    "disruptionPercentage": 0.0,
    "activatedEmployees": 2,
    "assignedMandatoryShifts": 8,
    "assignedOptionalShifts": 0,
    "travelDistance": 0
  }
}
```
When the `satisfiability` of the rule is `PREFERRED`, the `Shifts worked per period not in preferred range for employee` soft constraint is invoked.

With a `satisfiability` of `PREFERRED` a `shiftsWorkedMin` value can also be provided to set the preferred minimum number of shifts worked.

| `REQUIRED`satisfiability is not supported with `shiftsWorkedMin'. | 

```
{
  "contracts": [
    {
      "id": "partTimeContract",
      "periodRules": [
        {
          "id": "Min2ShiftsMax4ShiftsPerWeek",
          "satisfiability": "PREFERRED",
          "period": "WEEK",
          "shiftsWorkedMin": 2,
          "shiftsWorkedMax": 4
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
The `Shifts worked per period not in preferred range for employee` soft constraint is invoked when `satisfiability` is `PREFERRED` and an employee’s assigned shift count in a period is below `shiftsWorkedMin` or above `shiftsWorkedMax`.

The constraint adds a soft penalty to the dataset score when this preferred range is violated. The penalty is the number of shifts outside the preferred range multiplied by the employee priority multiplier and the contract’s priority weight, presented as minutes, incentivizing Timefold to keep shift counts within preferred limits.

Shifts will still be assigned even if assigning them breaks this constraint.

| Every soft constraint has a weight that can be configured to change the relative importance of the constraint compared to other constraints. | 

| This rule is more likely to be satisfied for employees with a higher employee priority.
See [Employee priority](https://docs.timefold.ai/employee-priority)for more details. | 

In the following example, Ann and Beth both work a preferred minimum of 2 shifts and a preferred maximum of 4 shifts per week. There are 10 shifts over 5 days. Ann is assigned 6 shifts and Beth is assigned 4 shifts.

Rules with a satisfiability of `REQUIRED` put a hard limit on how much work employees can be assigned (minutes, hours, days, shifts), and doesn’t assign overtime.

A rule with a satisfiability of `REQUIRED` that states an employee can work a maximum of 4 shifts per period, will never assign the employee more than 4 shifts per period, even if assigning overtime would be beneficial to the overall schedule.

To allow for the possibility of overtime, use rules with a satisfiability of `PREFERRED`.

Set a rule with a `PREFERRED` satisfiability for the maximum number of shifts per period.
Now, a rule with a satisfiability of `PREFERRED` that states an employee can preferably work a maximum of 4 shifts per period will allow the employee to be assigned more shifts per period (overtime) than specified by the rule when it is necessary to do so.

To place a limit on the total amount of overtime employees can be assigned, include both:

- 
A rule with `PREFERRED`satisfiability for the maximum number of shifts per period that is equivalent to the employees normal shifts per period.
- 
A rule with `REQUIRED`satisfiability for the maximum number of shifts per period (regular hours plus overtime).

The difference between the `PREFERRED` maximum shifts per period and `REQUIRED` maximum shifts per period is the total amount of overtime that can be assigned to employees.

# Weekend minutes worked per period

Source: https://docs.timefold.ai/employee-shift-scheduling/1.28.x/employee-resource-constraints/work-limits/weekend-minutes-worked-per-period.html

# Weekend minutes worked per period

There are different techniques for managing employees' working hours.

Weekend minutes worked per period rules puts a limit on how often employees work on weekends, for instance, if employees should only work 960 minutes (or 16 hours) on weekends throughout a period of 1 month.

Period rules for weekends can be defined for a month or the entire schedule.

This guide explains managing employees' hours with weekend minutes worked per period:

| ## Learn how to configure an API Key to run the examples in this guide:
 In the examples, replace  | 

Period rules are defined in contracts:

```
{
  "contracts": [
    {
      "id": "fullTimeContract",
      "periodRules": [
        {
          "id": "Max16WeekendHoursPerMonth",
          "period": "MONTH",
          "weekendsLimit":
          {
            "weekendMinutesWorkedMax": 960
          },
          "satisfiability": "REQUIRED"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
Period rules can define how many weekend minutes employees work in a given period, for instance, 960 minutes (16 hours) per month.

`PeriodRules` must include an ID.

`period` sets the period the rule applies to, for instance, `DAY`, `WEEK`, `MONTH`, `SCHEDULE`.

## Further information about `period`:

`DAY` spans a single day and occurs every day in the schedule.

`WEEK` spans 7 days and occurs every week (including partial weeks) in the schedule.
The default start of the week is Monday, but this can be overridden to any day in the week:

```
{
  "scheduleParameterization": {
    "weekStart": "THURSDAY"
  }
}
```
`MONTH` spans the entire month.
`MONTH` has a variable number of days depending on the days in the month and occurs every month (including partial months) in the schedule.

`SCHEDULE` spans the entire schedule.

| You can define custom periods to apply to this rule in the following way: | 

```
{
  "scheduleParameterization": {
    "periods": [
      {
        "id": "PAY_PERIOD",
        "dateSpans": [
          {
            "start": "2023-01-01",
            "end": "2023-01-15"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```
The `start` and `end` dates are inclusive.

| `weekendsLimit`rules can only be defined for periods`MONTH`or`SCHEDULE`. | 

## Learn about counting days in rules:

By default, rules count shifts within the defined period or rolling window if the shift starts within it. For instance, if you define a rule that an employee can only work one shift per day, a night shift that started on the previous day but ends the following morning will not be counted towards the limits specified in the rule.

To change this behavior, change the field `periodShiftOverlapKind` from `START_ONLY` to `START_AND_END`.

- 
Period rule 
- 
Rolling-window rule 

```
{
  "periodRules": [
    {
      "id": "Max8HoursPerDayFullTime",
      "period": "DAY",
      "minutesWorkedLimit": {
        "minutesWorkedMax": 480
      },
      "satisfiability": "REQUIRED",
      "periodShiftOverlapKind": "START_AND_END"
    }
  ]
}
```
```
{
  "rollingWindowRules": [
    {
      "id": "Max8HoursPerDayRolling",
      "rollingWindow": {
        "type": "DAILY",
        "size": 1
      },
      "minutesWorkedLimit": {
        "minutesWorkedMax": 480
      },
      "satisfiability": "REQUIRED",
      "periodShiftOverlapKind": "START_AND_END"
    }
  ]
}
```
This makes the rule count all parts of shifts that overlap with the defined period or rolling window. In the previous example, the night shift starts on the previous day and ends the following morning. With `START_AND_END`, the portion of the night shift that overlaps the target period or window is counted toward the rule.

The default behavior of all rules when this field is not specified is `START_ONLY`.

The `weekendsLimit` object must include `weekendMinutesWorkedMax` with the maximum number of weekend minutes worked per period.

By default, breaks in shifts do not count towards working time. It is possible to specify which breaks are subtracted from working time for the rule by using `unloggedBreakTags`.

## Further information about subtracting breaks from working time based on tags:

Breaks with specific tags are not logged towards the working time of this rule. Tags are defined in shift breaks:

```
{
  "shifts": [
    {
      "id": "shift 1",
      "start": "2027-02-01T09:00:00Z",
      "end": "2027-02-01T18:00:00Z",
      "breaks": [
        {
          "start": "2027-02-01T10:30:00Z",
          "end": "2027-02-01T10:45:00Z",
          "tags": ["teaBreak"]
        },
        {
          "start": "2027-02-01T12:00:00Z",
          "end": "2027-02-01T13:00:00Z",
          "tags": ["lunchBreak"]
        },
        {
          "start": "2027-02-01T16:30:00Z",
          "end": "2027-02-01T16:45:00Z",
          "tags": ["teaBreak"]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
Use `unloggedBreakTags` to specify which breaks are subtracted from the working time for this rule.
Breaks which do not match the tags will be counted as working time.
Do not use this field if all breaks must be subtracted from working time, regardless of their tags.

`breakTagMatches` can be set to `ALL` or `ANY`.
The default behavior for `breakTagMatches` is `ALL`, and if omitted, the default `ALL` will be used.

The rule can define only `unloggedBreakTags`.

```
{
  "unloggedBreakTags": ["lunchBreak"],
  "breakTagMatches": "ALL"
}
```
In the above example, breaks which have the tag `lunchBreak` will be subtracted from working time for the rule. All other breaks will count as working time.

With `breakTagMatches` set to `ALL`, all tags defined by the rule’s `unloggedBreakTags` attribute must be present in the break in order for it to be subtracted from working time.
With `breakTagMatches` set to `ANY`, at least one tag defined by the rule’s `unloggedBreakTags` attribute must be present in the break.

Each employee must specify which contracts apply to them:

```
{
  "employees": [
    {
      "id": "Ann",
      "contracts": [
        "fullTimeContract"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
`periodRules` can include or exclude shifts based on shift tags.

```
{
  "contracts": [
    {
      "id": "fullTimeContract",
      "periodRules": [
        {
          "id": "Max16WeekendHoursPerMonth",
          "period": "MONTH",
          "includeShiftTags": ["Part-time"],
          "shiftTagMatches": "ALL",
          "weekendsLimit":
          {
            "weekendMinutesWorkedMax": 960
          },
          "satisfiability": "REQUIRED"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
## Further information about including or excluding shifts with shift tags:

Shifts with specific tags can be included or excluded by the rule. Tags are defined in shifts:

```
{
  "shifts": [
    {
      "id": "2027-02-01",
      "start": "2027-02-01T09:00:00Z",
      "end": "2027-02-01T17:00:00Z",
      "tags": ["Part-time"]
    }
  ]
}
```
Use `includeShiftTags` to include shifts with specific tags or  `excludeShiftTags` to exclude shifts with specific tags.

`shiftTagMatches` can be set to `ALL` or `ANY`.
The default behavior for `shiftTagMatches` is `ALL`, and if omitted, the default `ALL` will be used.

The rule can define either `includeShiftTags` or `excludeShiftTags`, but not both.

```
{
  "includeShiftTags": ["Part-time", "Weekend"],
  "shiftTagMatches": "ALL"
}
```
With `shiftTagMatches` set to `ALL`, all tags defined by the rule’s `includeShiftTags` attribute must be present in the shift. With `shiftTagMatches` set to `ANY`, at least one tag defined by the rule’s `includeShiftTags` attribute must be present in the shift.

```
{
  "excludeShiftTags": ["Part-time", "Weekend"],
  "shiftTagMatches": "ALL"
}
```
With `shiftTagMatches` set to `ALL`, all tags defined by the rule’s `excludeShiftTags` attribute cannot be present in the shift.
This is useful when you want to exclude things in combination with each other.
For instance, excluding the shift tags `Part-time` and `Weekend` with `shiftTagMatches` set to `All`, will exclude shifts that include the tags `Part-time` and `Weekend` from the rule.
Shifts tagged only `Part-time` or only `Weekend` will not be excluded.

With `shiftTagMatches` set to `ANY`, any of the tags defined by the rule’s `excludeShiftTags` attribute cannot be present in the shift.
This is useful when you need to exclude tags regardless of their relationship to other tags.
For instance, excluding the shift tags `Part-time` and `Weekend` with `shiftTagMatches` set to `ANY`, will exclude any shift that includes the tags `Part-time` or `Weekend`, whether they occur together or not.

By default, weekends are Saturday and Sunday.

You can define different weekend days. Weekend days must be consecutive and have a maximum of three days and a minimum of one day.

Weekend days are configured in contracts:

```
{
  "contracts": [
    {
      "id": "fullTimeContract",
      "weekendConfiguration": {
        "weekendDays": [
          "FRIDAY",
          "SATURDAY"
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
When the satisfiability of the rule is `REQUIRED`, the `Weekend minutes worked per period not in required range for employee` hard constraint is invoked, which makes sure the number of weekend minutes worked per period does not exceed the limit specified in `weekendMinutesWorkedMax`.

Shifts will be left unassigned if assigning them would break the `Weekend minutes worked per period not in required range for employee` constraint.

In the following example, there are 8 shifts, 1 employee, and a rule with a required satisfiability that specifies the employee can work at most 960 weekend minutes (16 hours) per month.

| Only the weekend shifts are shown in the example. | 

2 shifts, totaling 960 minutes, are assigned and 6 shifts are left unassigned to avoid breaking the `Weekend minutes worked per period not in required range for employee` hard constraint.

The `Weekend minutes Worked Per Period Not In Preferred Range For Employee` soft constraint is invoked when `satisfiability` is `PREFERRED` and weekend minutes worked in the period exceed `weekendMinutesWorkedMax`.

The constraint adds a soft penalty to the dataset score that is calculated as the number of weekend minutes above `weekendMinutesWorkedMax` multiplied by the employee priority multiplier and the contract’s priority weight, incentivizing Timefold to keep weekend minutes worked within the preferred limit.

Shifts will still be assigned even if assigning them breaks this constraint.

| Every soft constraint has a weight that can be configured to change the relative importance of the constraint compared to other constraints. | 

| This rule is more likely to be satisfied for employees with a higher employee priority.
See [Employee priority](https://docs.timefold.ai/employee-priority)for more details. | 

In the following example, there are 8 shifts, 1 employee, and a rule with a preferred satisfiability that specifies the employee should work at most 960 weekend minutes (16 hours) per month.

All 8 shifts are assigned, totaling 3,840 minutes, and a soft penalty is applied to the dataset score.

Rules with a satisfiability of `REQUIRED` put a hard limit on how much work employees can be assigned (minutes, hours, days, shifts), and doesn’t assign overtime.

A rule with a satisfiability of `REQUIRED` that states an employee can work a maximum of 960 weekend minutes per period, will never assign the employee more than 960 weekend minutes per period, even if assigning overtime would be beneficial to the overall schedule.

To allow for the possibility of overtime, use rules with a satisfiability of `PREFERRED`.

Set a rule with a `PREFERRED` satisfiability for the maximum number of weekend minutes per period.
Now, a rule with a satisfiability of `PREFERRED` that states an employee can preferably work a maximum of 960 weekend minutes per period will allow the employee to be assigned more weekend minutes per period (overtime) than specified by the rule when it is necessary to do so.

To place a limit on the total amount of overtime employees can be assigned, include both:

- 
A rule with `PREFERRED`satisfiability for the maximum number of weekend minutes per period that is equivalent to the employees normal weekend minutes per period.
- 
A rule with `REQUIRED`satisfiability for the maximum number of weekend minutes per period (regular hours plus overtime).

The difference between the `PREFERRED` maximum weekend minutes per period and `REQUIRED` maximum weekend minutes per period is the total amount of overtime that can be assigned to employees.

# Weekends worked in a rolling window

Source: https://docs.timefold.ai/employee-shift-scheduling/1.28.x/employee-resource-constraints/work-limits/weekends-worked-in-a-rolling-window.html

# Weekends worked in a rolling window

There are different techniques for managing employees working hours.

Rolling windows can be defined as hourly, daily, or weekly.

This guide explains managing employees' hours with weekends worked in a rolling window.

| ## Learn how to configure an API Key to run the examples in this guide:
 In the examples, replace  | 

Rolling window rules are defined in contracts:

```
{
  "contracts": [
    {
      "id": "fullTimeContract",
      "rollingWindowRules": [
        {
          "id": "max1WeekendRollingWindow",
          "rollingWindow": {
            "type": "WEEKLY",
            "size": 4
          },
          "weekendsLimit":
          {
            "weekendsWorkedMax": 1
          },
          "satisfiability": "REQUIRED"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
This rule specifies a rolling window of 4 weeks.

You can define as many `rollingWindowRules` as required.

`rollingWindowRules` must include an ID.

`rollingWindow` specifies the `type` and `size` of the window.

## Further information about `rollingWindows`:

`size` sets how many instances of `type` are included in the rolling window, for instance, the following example specifies a rolling window of 7 days.

```
{
  "rollingWindow": {
    "type": "DAILY",
    "size": 7
  }
}
```
There are three types of rolling windows `HOURLY`, `DAILY`, and `WEEKLY`.

The type specifies how the rolling window progress, hour-by-hour, day-by-day, or week-by-week.

- 
`HOURLY`spans the number of hours specified in`size`and occurs every hour when shifts are scheduled. The hourly window starts when a shift starts (for example 8:00, or 14:30)
- 
`DAILY`spans the number of days specified in`size`for 24-hour periods and covers the entire schedule. The daily window starts at the beginning of a calendar day (midnight).
- 
`WEEKLY`spans the number of weeks specified in`size`and occurs every week (including partial weeks) in the schedule. The weekly window starts at the beginning of a calendar week (usually Monday, or Sunday).

By default, the start of the week is Monday, however, this can be overridden for the entire schedule:

```
{
  "scheduleParameterization": {
    "weekStart": "THURSDAY"
  }
}
```
| Changing `weekStart`is a global change that applies to the entire dataset. | 

The `weekendsLimit` object must include `weekendsWorkedMax` or `weekendsWorkedMin` with respectively the maximum number and minimum number of weekends to work in the rolling window.

## Learn about counting days in rules:

By default, rules count shifts within the defined period or rolling window if the shift starts within it. For instance, if you define a rule that an employee can only work one shift per day, a night shift that started on the previous day but ends the following morning will not be counted towards the limits specified in the rule.

To change this behavior, change the field `periodShiftOverlapKind` from `START_ONLY` to `START_AND_END`.

- 
Period rule 
- 
Rolling-window rule 

```
{
  "periodRules": [
    {
      "id": "Max8HoursPerDayFullTime",
      "period": "DAY",
      "minutesWorkedLimit": {
        "minutesWorkedMax": 480
      },
      "satisfiability": "REQUIRED",
      "periodShiftOverlapKind": "START_AND_END"
    }
  ]
}
```
```
{
  "rollingWindowRules": [
    {
      "id": "Max8HoursPerDayRolling",
      "rollingWindow": {
        "type": "DAILY",
        "size": 1
      },
      "minutesWorkedLimit": {
        "minutesWorkedMax": 480
      },
      "satisfiability": "REQUIRED",
      "periodShiftOverlapKind": "START_AND_END"
    }
  ]
}
```
This makes the rule count all parts of shifts that overlap with the defined period or rolling window. In the previous example, the night shift starts on the previous day and ends the following morning. With `START_AND_END`, the portion of the night shift that overlaps the target period or window is counted toward the rule.

The default behavior of all rules when this field is not specified is `START_ONLY`.

`RollingWindowRules` can include or exclude shifts based on tags.

```
{
  "rollingWindowRules": [
    {
      "id": "max1WeekendRollingWindow",
      "includeShiftTags": ["Part-time"],
      "shiftTagMatches": "ALL",
      "rollingWindow": {
        "type": "WEEKLY",
        "size": 4
      },
      "weekendsLimit":
      {
        "weekendsWorkedMax": 2
      },
      "satisfiability": "REQUIRED"
    }
  ]
}
```
## Further information about including or excluding shifts with shift tags:

Shifts with specific tags can be included or excluded by the rule. Tags are defined in shifts:

```
{
  "shifts": [
    {
      "id": "2027-02-01",
      "start": "2027-02-01T09:00:00Z",
      "end": "2027-02-01T17:00:00Z",
      "tags": ["Part-time"]
    }
  ]
}
```
Use `includeShiftTags` to include shifts with specific tags or  `excludeShiftTags` to exclude shifts with specific tags.

`shiftTagMatches` can be set to `ALL` or `ANY`.
The default behavior for `shiftTagMatches` is `ALL`, and if omitted, the default `ALL` will be used.

The rule can define either `includeShiftTags` or `excludeShiftTags`, but not both.

```
{
  "includeShiftTags": ["Part-time", "Weekend"],
  "shiftTagMatches": "ALL"
}
```
With `shiftTagMatches` set to `ALL`, all tags defined by the rule’s `includeShiftTags` attribute must be present in the shift. With `shiftTagMatches` set to `ANY`, at least one tag defined by the rule’s `includeShiftTags` attribute must be present in the shift.

```
{
  "excludeShiftTags": ["Part-time", "Weekend"],
  "shiftTagMatches": "ALL"
}
```
With `shiftTagMatches` set to `ALL`, all tags defined by the rule’s `excludeShiftTags` attribute cannot be present in the shift.
This is useful when you want to exclude things in combination with each other.
For instance, excluding the shift tags `Part-time` and `Weekend` with `shiftTagMatches` set to `All`, will exclude shifts that include the tags `Part-time` and `Weekend` from the rule.
Shifts tagged only `Part-time` or only `Weekend` will not be excluded.

With `shiftTagMatches` set to `ANY`, any of the tags defined by the rule’s `excludeShiftTags` attribute cannot be present in the shift.
This is useful when you need to exclude tags regardless of their relationship to other tags.
For instance, excluding the shift tags `Part-time` and `Weekend` with `shiftTagMatches` set to `ANY`, will exclude any shift that includes the tags `Part-time` or `Weekend`, whether they occur together or not.

By default, weekends are Saturday and Sunday.

You can define different weekend days. Weekend days must be consecutive and have a maximum of three days and a minimum of one day.

Weekend days are configured in contracts:

```
{
  "contracts": [
    {
      "id": "fullTimeContract",
      "weekendConfiguration": {
        "weekendDays": [
          "FRIDAY",
          "SATURDAY"
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
When the satisfiability of the rule is `REQUIRED`, the `Weekends worked in rolling window not in required range for employeee` hard constraint is invoked, which makes sure the number of weekends worked in the rolling window is not above the limit specified in `weekendsWorkedMax`.
The `weekendsWorkedMin` is not available when the satisfiability of the rule is `REQUIRED`.

Shifts will be left unassigned if assigning them would break the `Weekends worked in rolling window not in required range for employee` constraint.

In the following example, there are 8 shifts, 1 employee, and a rule with a required satisfiability that states the employee cannot work more than 1 weekend in a 4-week rolling window.

2 shifts are assigned, and 6 shifts are left unassigned to avoid breaking the `Weekends worked in rolling window not in required range for employee` hard constraint.

```
{
  "contracts": [
    {
      "id": "fullTimeContract",
      "rollingWindowRules": [

          },

The `Weekends worked in rolling window not in preferred range for employee` soft constraint is invoked when `satisfiability` is `PREFERRED` and the number of weekends worked within the rolling window is below `weekendsWorkedMin` or above `weekendsWorkedMax`.

The constraint adds a soft penalty to the dataset score that is calculated as the number of weekends outside the preferred range multiplied by the employee priority multiplier and the contract’s priority weight, normalized to minutes, incentivizing Timefold to keep weekend assignments within the preferred limits.

Shifts will still be assigned even if assigning them breaks this constraint.

| Every soft constraint has a weight that can be configured to change the relative importance of the constraint compared to other constraints. | 

| This rule is more likely to be satisfied for employees with a higher employee priority.
See [Employee priority](https://docs.timefold.ai/employee-priority)for more details. |

You can define a condition that has to be fulfilled in the rolling window before the rolling window rule is evaluated.

`condition` specifies the `triggerLimit`, `type` and `includeShiftTags`.

## Further information about `conditions`:

`type` sets the `triggerLimit` unit, for instance, the example below requires at least two shifts to be worked with the tag `Night shift` in the rolling window before the condition is activated.
The `type` can either be `MIN_SHIFTS_WORKED` or `MIN_MINUTES_WORKED`.

```
{
  "condition": {
    "triggerLimit": 2,
    "type": "MIN_SHIFTS_WORKED"
  }
}
```
`includeShiftTags` can be used to only include specific shifts. The example below limits the two shifts worked to "night shifts".

```
{
  "condition": {
    "triggerLimit": 2,
    "type": "MIN_SHIFTS_WORKED",
    "includeShiftTags": [ "Night shift" ]
  }
}
```
For example, an employee must work at most one weekend in a rolling window, if they worked at least three night shifts in that rolling window.

```
{
  "contracts": [
    {
      "id": "limitWeekendShiftsWhen3NightShiftWereWorked",
      "rollingWindowRules": [
        {
          "id": "1WeekendWorkedRollingWindow",
          "rollingWindow": {
            "type": "WEEKLY",
            "size": 2
          },
          "weekendsLimit": {
            "weekendsWorkedMax": 1
          },
          "satisfiability": "REQUIRED",
          "condition": {
            "triggerLimit": 3,
            "type": "MIN_SHIFTS_WORKED",
            "includeShiftTags": [ "night shift" ]
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

# Weekends worked per period

Source: https://docs.timefold.ai/employee-shift-scheduling/1.28.x/employee-resource-constraints/work-limits/weekends-worked-per-period.html

# Weekends worked per period

There are different techniques for managing employees' working hours.

Weekends worked per period rules limit how many weekends employees can work in a period, for instance, if employees should only work 1 weekend throughout a period of 1 month.

Period rules for weekends can be defined for a month or the entire schedule.

This guide explains managing employees' hours with weekends worked per period:

| ## Learn how to configure an API Key to run the examples in this guide:
 In the examples, replace  | 

Period rules are defined in contracts:

```
{
  "contracts": [
    {
      "id": "fullTimeContract",
      "periodRules": [
        {
          "id": "Max1WeekendPerMonth",
          "period": "MONTH",
          "weekendsLimit":
          {
            "weekendsWorkedMax": 1
          },
          "satisfiability": "REQUIRED"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
Period rules can define how many weekends employees work in a given period, for instance, 1 weekend per month.

`PeriodRules` must include an ID.

`period` sets the period the rule applies to, for instance, `DAY`, `WEEK`, `MONTH`, `SCHEDULE`.

## Further information about `period`:

`DAY` spans a single day and occurs every day in the schedule.

`WEEK` spans 7 days and occurs every week (including partial weeks) in the schedule.
The default start of the week is Monday, but this can be overridden to any day in the week:

```
{
  "scheduleParameterization": {
    "weekStart": "THURSDAY"
  }
}
```
`MONTH` spans the entire month.
`MONTH` has a variable number of days depending on the days in the month and occurs every month (including partial months) in the schedule.

`SCHEDULE` spans the entire schedule.

| You can define custom periods to apply to this rule in the following way: | 

```
{
  "scheduleParameterization": {
    "periods": [
      {
        "id": "PAY_PERIOD",
        "dateSpans": [
          {
            "start": "2023-01-01",
            "end": "2023-01-15"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```
The `start` and `end` dates are inclusive.

| `weekendsLimit`rules can only be defined for periods`MONTH`or`SCHEDULE`. | 

## Learn about counting days in rules:

By default, rules count shifts within the defined period or rolling window if the shift starts within it. For instance, if you define a rule that an employee can only work one shift per day, a night shift that started on the previous day but ends the following morning will not be counted towards the limits specified in the rule.

To change this behavior, change the field `periodShiftOverlapKind` from `START_ONLY` to `START_AND_END`.

- 
Period rule 
- 
Rolling-window rule 

```
{
  "periodRules": [
    {
      "id": "Max8HoursPerDayFullTime",
      "period": "DAY",
      "minutesWorkedLimit": {
        "minutesWorkedMax": 480
      },
      "satisfiability": "REQUIRED",
      "periodShiftOverlapKind": "START_AND_END"
    }
  ]
}
```
```
{
  "rollingWindowRules": [
    {
      "id": "Max8HoursPerDayRolling",
      "rollingWindow": {
        "type": "DAILY",
        "size": 1
      },
      "minutesWorkedLimit": {
        "minutesWorkedMax": 480
      },
      "satisfiability": "REQUIRED",
      "periodShiftOverlapKind": "START_AND_END"
    }
  ]
}
```
This makes the rule count all parts of shifts that overlap with the defined period or rolling window. In the previous example, the night shift starts on the previous day and ends the following morning. With `START_AND_END`, the portion of the night shift that overlaps the target period or window is counted toward the rule.

The default behavior of all rules when this field is not specified is `START_ONLY`.

The `weekendsLimit` object must include `weekendsWorkedMax` with the maximum number of weekend worked per period.

Each employee must specify which contracts apply to them:

```
{
  "employees": [
    {
      "id": "Ann",
      "contracts": [
        "fullTimeContract"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
`periodRules` can include or exclude shifts based on tags.

```
{
  "contracts": [
    {
      "id": "fullTimeContract",
      "periodRules": [
        {
          "id": "Max1WeekendPerMonth",
          "period": "MONTH",
          "includeShiftTags": ["Part-time"],
          "shiftTagMatches": "ALL",
          "weekendsLimit":
          {
            "weekendsWorkedMax": 1
          },
          "satisfiability": "REQUIRED"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
## Further information about including or excluding shifts with shift tags:

Shifts with specific tags can be included or excluded by the rule. Tags are defined in shifts:

```
{
  "shifts": [
    {
      "id": "2027-02-01",
      "start": "2027-02-01T09:00:00Z",
      "end": "2027-02-01T17:00:00Z",
      "tags": ["Part-time"]
    }
  ]
}
```
Use `includeShiftTags` to include shifts with specific tags or  `excludeShiftTags` to exclude shifts with specific tags.

`shiftTagMatches` can be set to `ALL` or `ANY`.
The default behavior for `shiftTagMatches` is `ALL`, and if omitted, the default `ALL` will be used.

The rule can define either `includeShiftTags` or `excludeShiftTags`, but not both.

```
{
  "includeShiftTags": ["Part-time", "Weekend"],
  "shiftTagMatches": "ALL"
}
```
With `shiftTagMatches` set to `ALL`, all tags defined by the rule’s `includeShiftTags` attribute must be present in the shift. With `shiftTagMatches` set to `ANY`, at least one tag defined by the rule’s `includeShiftTags` attribute must be present in the shift.

```
{
  "excludeShiftTags": ["Part-time", "Weekend"],
  "shiftTagMatches": "ALL"
}
```
With `shiftTagMatches` set to `ALL`, all tags defined by the rule’s `excludeShiftTags` attribute cannot be present in the shift.
This is useful when you want to exclude things in combination with each other.
For instance, excluding the shift tags `Part-time` and `Weekend` with `shiftTagMatches` set to `All`, will exclude shifts that include the tags `Part-time` and `Weekend` from the rule.
Shifts tagged only `Part-time` or only `Weekend` will not be excluded.

With `shiftTagMatches` set to `ANY`, any of the tags defined by the rule’s `excludeShiftTags` attribute cannot be present in the shift.
This is useful when you need to exclude tags regardless of their relationship to other tags.
For instance, excluding the shift tags `Part-time` and `Weekend` with `shiftTagMatches` set to `ANY`, will exclude any shift that includes the tags `Part-time` or `Weekend`, whether they occur together or not.

By default, weekends are Saturday and Sunday.

You can define different weekend days. Weekend days must be consecutive and have a maximum of three days and a minimum of one day.

Weekend days are configured in contracts:

```
{
  "contracts": [
    {
      "id": "fullTimeContract",
      "weekendConfiguration": {
        "weekendDays": [
          "FRIDAY",
          "SATURDAY"
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
When the satisfiability of the rule is `REQUIRED`, the `Weekends worked per period not in required range for employee` hard constraint is invoked, which makes sure the number of weekends worked per period does not exceed the limit specified in `weekendsWorkedMax`.

Shifts will be left unassigned if assigning them would break the `Weekends worked per period not in required range for employee` constraint.

In the following example, there are 8 shifts, 1 employee, and a rule with a required satisfiability that specifies the employee can work at most 1 weekend per month.

| Only the weekend shifts are shown in the example. | 

2 shifts on 1 weekend are assigned and 6 shifts are left unassigned to avoid breaking the `Weekends worked per period not in required range for employee` hard constraint.

When the satisfiability of the rule is `PREFERRED`, the `Weekends worked per period not in preferred range for employee` soft constraint is invoked.

```
{
  "contracts": [
    {
      "id": "fullTimeContract",
      "periodRules": [
        {
          "id": "Max1WeekendPerMonth",
          "period": "MONTH",
          "weekendsLimit":
          {
            "weekendsWorkedMax": 1
          },
          "satisfiability": "PREFERRED"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
The `Weekends worked per period not In preferred range for employee` soft constraint is invoked when `satisfiability` is `PREFERRED` and the number of worked weekends in the period exceeds `weekendsWorkedMax`.

The constraint adds a soft penalty to the dataset score that is calculated as the number of weekends above `weekendsWorkedMax` multiplied by the employee priority multiplier and the contract’s priority weight, normalized to minutes, incentivizing Timefold to keep weekends worked within the preferred limit.

Shifts will still be assigned even if assigning them breaks this constraint.

| Every soft constraint has a weight that can be configured to change the relative importance of the constraint compared to other constraints. | 

| This rule is more likely to be satisfied for employees with a higher employee priority.
See [Employee priority](https://docs.timefold.ai/employee-priority)for more details. | 

In the following example, there are 8 shifts, 1 employee, and a rule with a preferred satisfiability that specifies the employee should work at most 1 weekend per month.

All 8 shifts are assigned, and a soft penalty is applied to the dataset score.

Rules with a satisfiability of `REQUIRED` put a hard limit on how much work employees can be assigned (minutes, hours, days, shifts), and doesn’t assign overtime.

A rule with a satisfiability of `REQUIRED` that states an employee can work a maximum of 1 weekends per period, will never assign the employee more than 1 weekends per period, even if assigning overtime would be beneficial to the overall schedule.

To allow for the possibility of overtime, use rules with a satisfiability of `PREFERRED`.

Set a rule with a `PREFERRED` satisfiability for the maximum number of weekends per period.
Now, a rule with a satisfiability of `PREFERRED` that states an employee can preferably work a maximum of 1 weekends per period will allow the employee to be assigned more weekends per period (overtime) than specified by the rule when it is necessary to do so.

To place a limit on the total amount of overtime employees can be assigned, include both:

- 
A rule with `PREFERRED`satisfiability for the maximum number of weekends per period that is equivalent to the employees normal weekends per period.
- 
A rule with `REQUIRED`satisfiability for the maximum number of weekends per period (regular hours plus overtime).

The difference between the `PREFERRED` maximum weekends per period and `REQUIRED` maximum weekends per period is the total amount of overtime that can be assigned to employees.
